1) Ca2+ is an important regulator of renin release and AII production; 2) Ca2+ can regulate the release of vasodilator PGE2 and the vasoconstrictor PGF2a from the kidney and 3) the Ca2+ induced alterations of the renin-aldosterone-vascular tone axis may contribute to the pathogenesis of hypertension.

Ca2+ is an important regulator of Bp, that the effects of Ca2+ on Bp are mediated through interactions with the rennin-angiotensn and prostaglandins systems, and that Ca2+ plays an important role in regulating renal blood flow and renal function.

the effects of Ca2+ on the release and activity of AII, renin, PGF2 and PGE2.
the role of Ca2+ in the regulation of Bp, renal blood flow, renin release, and renal and adrenal PG synthesis and metabolism.
the role of Ca2+ in the regulation of Bp and renal function.

Ca2+ plays a major role in the regulation of vascular tone, and that Ca2+ is an important modulator of the renin- angiotensin system.
Ca2+ has a complex regulatory role in the regulation of Bp.
Ca2+ has multiple effects on Bp, and these effects are mediated by complex interactions between Ca2+, renin, angiotensin and PGs.

calcium is a major regulator of renin release.
